stories.headline: ARC-AGI-3 Launches as Interactive Benchmark, Frontier LLMs Score Below 1%

key_facts.fact: ARC-AGI-3 launched on March 25, 2026 as a fundamentally new benchmark that abandons static grid puzzles for interactive, video-game-like environments where AI agents must discover rules and solve problems with zero instructions.
key_facts.excerpt: ARC-AGI-3, launched just yesterday on March 25, 2026, represents the most radical transformation of the ARC benchmark since François Chollet introduced it in 2019 — abandoning static grid puzzles entirely in favor of interactive, video-game-like environments where AI agents must discover rules, set goals, and solve problems with zero instructions.

key_facts.fact: Frontier LLMs including GPT-5 and Claude score below 1%, while simple CNN and graph-search approaches reach 12.58%, with human performance at 100%.
key_facts.excerpt: Early preview results: frontier LLMs like GPT-5 and Claude score below 1%, while simple CNN and graph-search approaches reach 12.58%. The gap between human performance (100%) and the best AI agent remains enormous.

key_facts.fact: The competition carries over $2 million in prizes across three tracks, with $700K grand prize for a 100% score and submissions due November 2, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: The competition carries over $2 million in prizes across three tracks.

key_facts.fact: The benchmark contains 1,000+ levels across 150+ handcrafted environments, where agents enter 64x64 grid worlds with 16 colors and must learn through trial-and-error.
key_facts.excerpt: The benchmark contains '1,000+ levels across 150+ handcrafted environments.'

key_facts.fact: ARC-AGI-3 measures intelligence across time, not just final answers, capturing planning horizons, memory compression, and the ability to update beliefs as new evidence appears.
key_facts.excerpt: ARC-AGI-3 makes that gap measurable by testing intelligence across time, not just final answers—capturing planning horizons, memory compression, and the ability to update beliefs as new evidence appears.

stories.headline: Google Introduces TurboQuant: 6x LLM Memory Reduction and 8x Speedup at Zero Accuracy Loss

key_facts.fact: Google Research published TurboQuant, a data-oblivious quantization framework that compresses LLM key-value caches to 3 bits per value, reducing memory by 6x and delivering up to 8x speedup with no accuracy loss.
key_facts.excerpt: Google Research has developed three compression algorithms: TurboQuant, PolarQuant, and Quantized Johnson-Lindenstrauss (QJL). All three are designed to compress those caches aggressively without degrading model output quality.

key_facts.fact: TurboQuant combines PolarQuant, which converts Cartesian vectors to polar coordinates eliminating normalization overhead, with QJL which reduces residual errors to single sign bits with zero memory overhead.
key_facts.excerpt: PolarQuant handles the primary compression step by converting standard Cartesian coordinate vectors into polar coordinates. A conventional quantizer rec... TurboQuant addresses this by combining two underlying methods.

key_facts.fact: The algorithm was tested on Gemma and Mistral models running on NVIDIA H100 GPUs, achieving up to 8x performance boost over unquantized keys.
key_facts.excerpt: TurboQuant addresses this by combining two underlying methods. PolarQuant handles the primary compression step...

key_facts.fact: TurboQuant is data-oblivious, requiring no dataset-specific calibration for deployment, and was validated across LongBench, Needle In A Haystack, ZeroSCROLLS, RULER, and L-Eval benchmarks.
key_facts.excerpt: The persistent limitation of conventional approaches is that they require storing quantization constants in high precision for every small block of data, adding between one and two extra bits per number.

key_facts.fact: The compression enables powerful AI models to run locally on consumer devices like a 16GB Mac Mini or smartphones, according to coverage.
key_facts.excerpt: Google's TurboQuant reduces AI LLM cache memory capacity requirements by at least six times — up to 8x performance boost on Nvidia H100 GPUs, compresses KV caches to 3 bits with no accuracy loss

stories.headline: LiteLLM Supply Chain Attack Steals SSH Keys and Cloud Credentials From 95M-Download Package

key_facts.fact: On March 24, 2026, LiteLLM PyPI versions 1.82.7 and 1.82.8 were published with credential-stealing malware via a compromised maintainer account, part of the broader TeamPCP supply chain campaign.
key_facts.excerpt: On March 24, 2026, two PyPI releases of LiteLLM, 1.82.7 and 1.82.8, were published with malicious code as a result of a supply chain compromise.

key_facts.fact: The malicious .pth file auto-executed on every Python invocation without any import, stealing environment variables, SSH private keys, AWS/GCP/Azure/Kubernetes credentials, git configs, shell history, and crypto wallet files.
key_facts.excerpt: Python automatically runs .pth files in your site-packages directory every time the Python interpreter starts. No import needed, no user interaction. The attacker hid a double base64-encoded payload inside this file.

key_facts.fact: LiteLLM has approximately 95 million monthly downloads on PyPI and serves as a dependency for major AI frameworks including DSPy and CrewAI, amplifying the attack's blast radius.
key_facts.excerpt: LiteLLM gets 97 million downloads per month... it has over 95 million monthly downloads on PyPI and serves as a universal API gateway for over 100 LLM providers.

key_facts.fact: Datadog's investigation traced the attack to a five-day TeamPCP campaign that began with the March 19 Trivy compromise, continued through CanisterWorm on npm, then hit Checkmarx KICS before reaching LiteLLM.
key_facts.excerpt: The LiteLLM compromise is the latest event in a five-day campaign that began with the March 19 Trivy compromise, continued with CanisterWorm on npm, and then reached Checkmarx KICS and related artifacts.

key_facts.fact: The attack was discovered accidentally when a developer's machine crashed from RAM exhaustion caused by a bug in the malware that triggered an exponential fork bomb.
key_facts.excerpt: Callum McMahon's machine crashes from RAM exhaustion - a bug in the malware caused an exponential fork bomb, leading to discovery

key_facts.fact: PyPI quarantined the entire litellm package and LiteLLM is pausing new releases until completing a broader supply-chain review.
key_facts.excerpt: We are pausing new LiteLLM releases until we complete a broader supply-chain review and confirm the release path is safe.

stories.headline: OpenAI Publishes Model Spec Philosophy, the 100-Page Framework Governing ChatGPT

key_facts.fact: On March 25, 2026, OpenAI published a detailed blog post explaining the philosophy and mechanics behind its Model Spec, the 100-page document that defines how ChatGPT should behave across all queries.
key_facts.excerpt: This post shares the backstory that is not in the Model Spec itself, including the philosophy and mechanics behind it: how it's structured, why we made those structural choices, and how we write, implement, and evolve it over time.

key_facts.fact: The Model Spec defines how models should follow instructions, resolve conflicts, respect user freedom, and behave safely, functioning both as a description of current behavior and a target for improvement.
key_facts.excerpt: The Model Spec is our formal framework for model behavior. It defines how we want models to follow instructions, resolve conflicts, respect user freedom, and behave safely across the incredibly broad range of queries that users ask them daily.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI frames the document as an interface so that researchers, policymakers, and the public can read, inspect, and debate intended model behavior rather than it being hidden inside the training process.
key_facts.excerpt: We use it to make intended behavior clearer, so we can train toward it, evaluate against it, and improve it over time.

stories.headline: Ukrainian OSIRIS AI Unveils Combat-Tested UEB-1 AI Interceptor Drone at 315 km/h

key_facts.fact: OSIRIS AI presented the UEB-1 interceptor drone at the Xpotential 2026 exhibition in Dusseldorf, Germany, designed to intercept high-speed aerial targets at up to 315 km/h.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukrainian developer OSIRIS AI unveiled its new UEB-1 interceptor drone, capable of reaching speeds of up to 315 km/h, at the Xpotential exhibition in Dusseldorf.

key_facts.fact: The drone uses the OSIRIS DroneOS platform with AI for autonomous trajectory prediction and object tracking, requiring minimal operator involvement.
key_facts.excerpt: The system uses artificial intelligence to predict where a target is going and to track it effectively.

key_facts.fact: Specs include 18 km flight range, 10+ minutes endurance, 3.1 kg total weight with 0.5 kg payload, and a carbon fiber frame measuring 370 x 370 x 550 mm.
key_facts.excerpt: The UEB-1's technical specifications include a flight range of up to 18 kilometers and an endurance of over 10 minutes. With a total weight of 3.1 kg, the drone carries a 0.5 kg payload.

key_facts.fact: The drone has been tested in combat conditions and is part of the OSIRIS AI ecosystem for countering aerial threats from the Russian Federation.
key_facts.excerpt: The flight range is up to 18 km, and the drone itself has already been tested in combat conditions. OSIRIS UEB-1 is reportedly part of the OSIRIS AI ecosystem for countering aerial threats.

key_facts.fact: OSIRIS AI has production facilities in Ukraine and Poland with an R&D center in Krakow, funded by foreign investment received in 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: OSIRIS AI's production facilities are located in Ukraine and Poland, and a research and development (R&D) center is located in Krakow.

sources.title: Ukraine Unveils AI-Powered UEB-1 Interceptor Drone Capable of 315 km/h

stories.headline: Iran Rejects US 15-Point Ceasefire Plan, Issues Own Five-Point Counterproposal

key_facts.fact: Iran dismissed the US 15-point ceasefire plan on March 25 and issued its own five-point counterproposal via state television
key_facts.excerpt: Iran on Wednesday dismissed the U.S. ceasefire plan and issued its own counterproposal

key_facts.fact: Iran's five demands include: halt to killings of Iranian officials, security guarantees against future wars, reparations for damages, end of hostilities, and sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz
key_facts.excerpt: Iran's counterproposal includes halt to killings of officials, security guarantees preventing future wars, reparations for war damages, end of hostilities, and control of Strait of Hormuz as Iran's exercise of sovereignty

key_facts.fact: A senior Iranian military spokesperson stated: 'People like us can never get along with people like you... no one like us will make a deal with you. Not now. Not ever.'
key_facts.excerpt: A senior military spokesperson stated: 'People like us can never get along with people like you… no one like us will make a deal with you. Not now. Not ever.'

key_facts.fact: Mediators are pursuing in-person talks, potentially Friday in Pakistan, though significant obstacles remain due to unclear authority within Iran's government and deep mutual distrust
key_facts.excerpt: Mediators are pursuing in-person talks, potentially Friday in Pakistan. However, significant obstacles remain: unclear authority within Iran's government and deep mutual distrust

key_facts.fact: War death toll stands at Iran 1,500+, Israel 20 (including 2 soldiers in Lebanon), US military 13+, Lebanon nearly 1,100, Iraq 80 security force members
key_facts.excerpt: Death toll: Iran: 1,500+; Israel: 20 (including 2 soldiers in Lebanon); U.S. military: 13+; Lebanon: Nearly 1,100; Iraq: 80 security force members

stories.headline: Iranian Drones Hit Kuwait International Airport Fuel Tank, Sparking Major Fire

key_facts.fact: Drones struck a fuel tank at Kuwait International Airport on March 25, triggering a fire that sent huge plumes of smoke over the area
key_facts.excerpt: Drones struck a fuel tank at Kuwait International Airport, triggering a fire

key_facts.fact: Kuwait's Directorate General of Civil Aviation reported only 'limited damage' with no casualties from the strike
key_facts.excerpt: The Directorate General of Civil Aviation reported the strike caused only 'limited damage' with no casualties

key_facts.fact: Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed responsibility, stating they launched missiles and drones at military bases hosting US forces in Kuwait, Jordan, and Bahrain
key_facts.excerpt: Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed responsibility, stating they had launched missiles and drones at military bases hosting US forces in Kuwait, Jordan, and Bahrain

key_facts.fact: The airport has been largely closed to commercial flights since the regional war began on February 28, with previous attacks on March 8 and March 14
key_facts.excerpt: The airport is largely closed to commercial flights and had already come under attack several times since the regional war began on February 28. Previous incidents occurred March 8 (fuel tank strikes) and March 14 (radar system damage)

stories.headline: Russian Drone Strikes Damage Lviv's UNESCO World Heritage Center

key_facts.excerpt: Buildings linked to the Bernardine Monastery complex were damaged. The city's historic center, listed as a UNESCO World Heritage site, was impacted

key_facts.fact: Several people were injured in the strikes, with emergency services deploying to contain fires in the historic center
key_facts.excerpt: Several people were injured. Emergency services deployed to the scene with visible smoke and fire

key_facts.fact: Other Ukrainian regions including Donetsk and Vinnytsia also reported strikes and casualties on the same day
key_facts.excerpt: Other Ukrainian regions (Donetsk, Vinnytsia) also reported strikes and casualties on the same date

key_facts.fact: Russia continued launching hundreds of drones at Ukraine on March 25 as part of its spring offensive, following a record barrage of nearly 1,000 in the preceding days

stories.headline: FDA Approves Denali's AVLAYAH, First New Hunter Syndrome Treatment in 20 Years

key_facts.fact: FDA approved AVLAYAH (tividenofusp alfa-eknm) on March 25 for neurologic manifestations of Hunter syndrome (MPS II) in pediatric patients, the first new treatment for the disease in nearly 20 years
key_facts.excerpt: Denali Therapeutics Announces U.S. FDA Approval of AVLAYAH (tividenofusp alfa-eknm). First new FDA-approved treatment option in nearly 20 years

key_facts.fact: Phase 1/2 trial of 47 participants showed 91% reduction in cerebrospinal fluid heparan sulfate by week 24, with 93% of patients (41 of 44) achieving normal-range levels
key_facts.excerpt: 91% reduction in cerebrospinal fluid heparan sulfate (CSF HS) by week 24. 93% of treated patients (41 of 44) achieved CSF HS levels within normal range

key_facts.fact: The drug uses Denali's TransportVehicle platform to cross the blood-brain barrier via receptor-mediated transcytosis, delivering enzyme replacement to the central nervous system
key_facts.excerpt: AVLAYAH fuses the IDS enzyme to Denali's TransportVehicle platform. The fusion protein binds transferrin receptors to cross the blood-brain barrier via receptor-mediated transcytosis

key_facts.fact: Hunter syndrome (MPS II) is a rare lysosomal storage disorder affecting approximately 500 individuals in the US; Denali received a Rare Pediatric Disease Priority Review Voucher
key_facts.excerpt: Rare lysosomal storage disorder affecting approximately 500 individuals in the U.S. Denali received a Rare Pediatric Disease Priority Review Voucher

sources.title: Denali Therapeutics Announces U.S. FDA Approval of AVLAYAH (tividenofusp alfa-eknm)

stories.headline: Beam Therapeutics Reports Strong Base Editing Results in Alpha-1 Antitrypsin Deficiency

key_facts.fact: BEAM-302, a base editing therapy that directly corrects the PiZ mutation in the SERPINA1 gene, showed mean steady-state AAT levels of 16.1 micromolar, consistently above the 11 micromolar protective threshold
key_facts.excerpt: Mean steady-state total AAT level: 16.1 µM (follow-up 5-12 months). All patients remained above protective threshold: 11 µM consistently and durably

key_facts.fact: Corrected M-AAT composition reached 94% of total AAT while mutant Z-AAT was reduced by 84% in 29 treated patients
key_facts.excerpt: Corrected M-AAT composition: 94% of total AAT. Mutant Z-AAT reduction: 84% decrease. 29 total treated patients

key_facts.fact: No serious adverse events or dose-limiting toxicities were reported across single doses up to 75 mg, with only mild to moderate adverse events observed
key_facts.excerpt: Well-tolerated across single doses up to 75 mg. No serious adverse events or dose-limiting toxicities reported

key_facts.fact: CEO John Evans called BEAM-302 a potential 'first- and best-in-class one-time treatment'; pivotal cohort of ~50 patients expected to begin enrollment in H2 2026 pursuing accelerated approval
key_facts.excerpt: CEO John Evans: 'These updated results reinforce the potential for BEAM-302 to become a first- and best-in-class one-time treatment.' Pivotal cohort enrollment (~50 additional patients) expected to initiate in second half of 2026

sources.title: Beam Therapeutics Announces Compelling Updated Clinical Data from the Ongoing Phase 1/2 Trial of BEAM-302 in Alpha-1 Antitrypsin Deficiency
